## 6a67124b-e88d-49da-aebe-ed9ee362dec4 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The unchanged PPO baseline learned a strong reach-and-hold policy late in training. The best measured checkpoint, `checkpoint-100352`, achieved 195/200 on the first research panel and 196/200 on a disjoint research panel, while the fixed task-reference panel measured 196/200. The final checkpoint was consistently weaker at 194/200 on both research panels and 194/200 on the reused task-reference panel. All nine failures of the selected checkpoint across the two research panels were in the approximately -150 to -121 degree target-angle sector, indicating a localized generalization gap. Development measurements do not establish the official objective.

**Lessons and limits:** Training-time success and reward tracked the emergence of useful task behavior, but they did not distinguish the best late checkpoints reliably: continued training after `checkpoint-100352` degraded measured success. The disjoint research panel confirms the selected checkpoint's near-threshold result without relying on the panel that first motivated selection. The fixed task-reference panel is corroborative but permanently reused, and all development measurements are distinct from the official 200-episode assessment. The baseline trained only on radii 14-20 cm, so the effect of broader radius coverage and concentrated exposure to the observed hard angle sector is unmeasured; evidence still covers one baseline training seed.

**Open questions:** Whether the selected policy reaches at least 98% on the official final panel remains unresolved. It is also unresolved whether the localized angular gap responds to targeted training coverage without degrading performance elsewhere.

**Current synthesis:** The unchanged PPO baseline learned a strong reach-and-hold policy, with `checkpoint-100352` scoring 195/200 and 196/200 on two research panels. On the newer disjoint panel, the retained working lineage scored 191/200 and the targeted transfer checkpoints scored 189/200, 190/200, and 187/200. The tested radius and hard-angle coverage intervention therefore did not improve the selected policy, and development measurements do not establish the official objective.

**Lessons and limits:** Training proxies tracked useful behavior but did not identify the best late checkpoint reliably; continuing beyond `checkpoint-100352` degraded measured success. Every measured transfer checkpoint was below the same-panel working control. This weakens that tested transfer recipe without ruling out other interventions or training variance. The fixed task-reference panel is reused, all development panels are distinct from the official assessment, and the campaign has only one fresh baseline run.

**Open questions:** Whether the selected policy reaches at least 98% on the official final panel remains unresolved. It is also unresolved whether unchanged learning from a fresh seed or a different scientific intervention can improve the residual generalization gap without degrading broad task performance.
